title: Deuxième partie : variations sur l'équation des lacets [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois…, pages 293 à 650, dont table des matières] : notes et copies de notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
This page continues a structural analysis (Grothendieck's pp. 459–460, archive p. 318) of the solution scheme G*_{ρ,σ} and its projectivised version G^{*~}_{ρ,σ} of the 'équation des lacets'. The setting is matrix groups G = GL2 and PG = PGL2 = GP(A). The loop equations take the form ξ = αρ(α)^{-1}, η = βσ(β)^{-1}, with twisting data ρ and σ; the next page specialises to ρ = [[0,1],[v,1]].

On the previous page Grothendieck obtained a parametrisation isomorphism (30): B̃'_0 × Ã_ρ × Ñ'_σ → G̃*_{ρ,σ}, given by (ũ,ã,b̃) ↦ (ũã^{-1}, ũb̃^{-1}, δ(ũ)). It uses three facts: B'_0 → PG is a monomorphism; A_ρ → PG and N'_σ → PG have kernel G_m; and T̃_ρ ∩ B̃'_0 = 1.

This page first defines the character δ on B̃'_0. Either δ(ũ) = det(u) for a lift u ∈ ΓB'_0 (31), or equivalently (cf. p. 441) δ(ũ) is the eigenvalue by which ũ acts on a distinguished element or line N_0, i.e. ũ(N_0) = δ(ũ)N_0 (32). Note that det is not well defined on PGL2 in general, so this uses the specific section B'_0 ⊂ GL2 mapping isomorphically onto its image. The coincidence of the two definitions is referred back to p. 441.

The Remark then gives the 'fibre' structure of the projection to the first coordinate. A section (α̃,β̃,μ) of G^{*~}_{ρ,σ} is determined by α̃ alone, up to the action of Ñ'_σ on β̃. The condition (locally) for α̃ to extend to a section is that the D-entry of ξ = αρ(α)^{-1} = [[A,B],[C,D]] be invertible. Then:
- μ = 1/D;
- η̃ = ξ̃ ε̃_1(μ−1), a correction by a unipotent/elementary matrix ε_1;
- β̃ is obtained by solving the Lang-type twisted equation β̃^σ (β̃^~)^{-1} = η̃. Its solutions form a torsor under Ñ'_σ.

The same holds for the unprojectivised G*_{ρ,σ} with sections (α,β,μ,ε). Here α alone determines the section mod N'_σ: from α one recovers u and a, hence μ = det u; then β = u b^{-1} with b ∈ ΓN'_σ arbitrary, and ε = ε(b).

Overall purpose: describe G*_{ρ,σ} as a principal N'_σ-bundle over an open subscheme (D invertible) of the α-space. This reduces the study of solutions to explicit polynomial conditions on α. The next page computes (−δv)D = −vd² + cd + c².
errors: No substantive mathematical error visible. Defining δ = det on PGL2 needs justification, since det is only defined up to squares there; it is legitimate because B'_0 → PG is a monomorphism, so ũ has a canonical lift. Grothendieck makes this explicit by giving the alternative definition via N_0.
The claim that a section is determined by α̃ 'mod Ñ'_σ' is stated locally ('loc^t'); globally the β̃ form a torsor, which need not have a section. Grothendieck flags this with 'loc^t'.

ideas.what: Character δ on the Borel-type subgroup B̃'_0 ⊂ PGL2 defined either via det of the canonical lift or via the eigenvalue on a fixed element N_0
ideas.modern_name: character of a Borel subgroup / eigencharacter on a stable line

ideas.what: Description of the solution scheme G*_{ρ,σ} as a torsor under N'_σ over the open locus where the D-coefficient of αρ(α)^{-1} is invertible, with β obtained from a Lang-type equation β^σ β^{-1} = η
ideas.modern_name: torsor / fibration structure of a twisted-conjugacy (Lang map) solution scheme
ideas.where_published: The 'équation des lacets' material belongs to the unpublished continuation of La Longue Marche; unsure whether any of it circulated

deep.surprise_reason: This is routine bookkeeping in an explicit GL2/PGL2 computation: a determinant character, and the fibre structure of a solution scheme over the α-coordinate. It belongs to the unpublished 'variations sur l'équation des lacets', but the content on this page is standard group-scheme manipulation with no new idea or connection.
transcription_corrections: Grothendieck's own page number appears to follow 459 (i.e. 460). The '350' at the top of the next-page transcription is likely a misreading of '460'.
In the Remark, the inserted phrase reads roughly 'reste, mod op. de Ñ'_σ sur β, déterminée, de façon précise, en termes de α̃'. The 'de' before G^{*~} is a correction from an 'eq.' or similar.
Final line: 'De même, une section (α, β, μ, ε) de G*_{ρ,σ} est déterminée par α seul mod N'_σ — on trouve d'abord u, a en termes [de α]'. The struck-out text before 'N'_σ' is illegible.

The marginal NBs are largely illegible. One appears to say that α̃ depends on fewer parameters than G^{*~}, since G^{*~}_{ρ,σ} ≅ B'_0 × Ã_ρ × Ñ'_σ. Another notes that locally α ∈ ΓG_1 depends on the choice of lifts ('dépend du choix des relèvements').
